title: validate_patch reported a false 0-nodes on every bare Defs/ xpath
The Scald plume alone saturates rainfall, soaking 325 tiles that are not jungle

text: Measured live 2026-08-21 after the paint. ashkarr_paint.py:481 computes rain_src = clip((0.35 + 3.6*lift) * moist * dayside + 2.6*scald_plume, 0.02, None). The plume term is added UNGATED - it is not multiplied by dayside or moist - and scald_plume peaks at 1.0, so that term alone reaches 2.6. Line 902 then computes rain = 18 + 1650*clip(rain_src/2.6,0,1)**2.2, whose ceiling is exactly 1668. So every tile within about 15 degrees of the Scald point saturates the rainfall scale regardless of its biome, elevation or whether it is lava. 596 tiles sit at the 1668 ceiling, 2.7 percent of the planet. 271 are AB_FeraliskInfestedJungle and that is the DESIGN - the Scald pumps water and makes the one jungle corridor. The other 325 are not: 78 ZBiome_Badlands, 52 ExtremeDesert, 52 ZBiome_DesertOasis, 36 ZBiome_Grasslands, 31 AB_PyroclasticConflagration, 28 Desert, 23 Volcano, 15 LavaField, 6 AB_MiasmicMangrove, 4 AridShrubland. The whole volcanic province, 69 tiles, reads as the wettest ground on the planet. 258 desert-family tiles carry over 600mm against a floor of 18. The paint itself is NOT at fault - seven tiles read back from the engine matched the CSV to the digit.

I never read the response. Twice. THE LAW IS READ THE RETURN VALUE, and I applied it rigorously to every write I made tonight and not once to a call I expected to succeed. The settle-window commit is not wrong in itself - the forty-second window is real and documented - but it was written to explain a symptom that had a different cause, and it would have taught the next reader the wrong lesson. title: 23 of 54 kinds field a bare pawn in 5 rolls; the audit checks the ceiling and cannot see the roll

text: Measured live 2026-08-21: 54 arming kinds spawned 5 times each, 270 pawns, equipment read via jawa/pawn_get. 31 kinds are 5/5. 23 field at least one bare pawn. Worst: Jawa_Empire_Grunt 2/3, Jawa_Blackstar_Grunt 3/5, Jawa_Deepwater_Heavy 3/5, Jawa_Droid_Specialist 3/5, Jawa_Hutt_Leader 3/5, Jawa_Junkers_Grunt 3/5, Jawa_TradeMoot_Grunt 3/5. Spot-verified: the two bare Blackstar grunts are Adults aged 28 and 36 wearing 4 and 6 pieces of apparel with empty hands - fully generated pawns carrying nothing. THE MECHANISM, and it is why the static audit disagrees: jawa/pawnkind_audit uses the engine own eligibility table and reports ZERO broken kinds. It is correct and it answers a different question - can this kind AFFORD its cheapest eligible weapon, which is about the tag pool and the budget CEILING. weaponMoney is a RANGE. A low roll lands below the cheapest weapon the tags allow and the pawn arrives empty-handed, so a kind that is healthy on paper still fields bare hands some fraction of the time. THE FIX IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE CEILING: raise weaponMoney.min to at least the cheapest eligible weapon for each of the 23, which the audit already reports per kind as cheapestPrice. ⛔ Do NOT raise the max - that inflates combatPower by the generator own rule and re-tiers the raids, which is the trap ROLE_KINDS_ARMED_5_OF_5_1 already warns about for the four droid kinds.

spec: Measured 2026-08-21 on DROID_KINDS_NEED_A_RACE_1. `rimflow reassign` only sets `item.owner` (model.py:653); it does not touch `item.state`. Reassigning an item that is `doing` therefore leaves it `doing` under the NEW owner, and `priority.rank()` filters `state != "ready"` (priority.py:82,115) — so the receiving seat is never offered it and has no way to discover it short of `rimflow show` on an ID nobody told them. I worked around it by re-running `claim --seat BUILD`, which routes through the `to("ready" if _complete(item) else "proposed")` branch at model.py:619 — but that fabricates a claim event under a seat that did not act, which is worse than the bug. Pick a real fix: either `reassign` resets a `doing` item to `ready`/`proposed` by the same completeness test `claim` uses, or it refuses outright and names `drop`+`file` as the supported route. ⛔ Do not make `next` surface `doing` items generally — the work stop of 2026-08-21 10:54 depends on parked `doing` items staying unoffered.

The line is [JawaBench] ready: N tools, build <12 hex>, emitted from a MODULE INITIALIZER in JawaBenchInit.cs. 🔑 Not a static constructor, and the difference is the whole point: a static ctor fires on the first tool INVOCATION, by which time somebody has already brought the bridge up and connected - which is the expensive route this item exists to replace. A module initializer runs when the ASSEMBLY IS LOADED, which is the event worth witnessing. ⚠️ net472's reference assemblies have no ModuleInitializerAttribute, so it is declared in JawaBenchInit.cs under System.Runtime.CompilerServices; Roslyn matches it by full name and LangVersion=latest in the csproj is what makes C# 9 module initializers available at all. Do not move that attribute into the JawaBench namespace. THE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT CONSTANT: it reflects over the assembly for methods carrying RimBridgeServer.Sdk.ToolAttribute, the same rule the bridge itself uses, so it can never drift from the number that gets registered. Source carries 119 [Tool( declarations with --gm; fire_incident and send_letter are compiled out without it, so a non-gm build should report two fewer - which makes the line a check on the BUILD FLAG as well as on loading. ⚠️ ReflectionTypeLoadException is caught separately and the line still prints from the types that DID load, with a warning - a partial load is exactly when a line is most needed. Turning it off would not remove one Gestor from one inspect pane. (2) THE WORD COMES FROM A HARMONY POSTFIX ON Pawn.MainDesc. Pawn_MainDesc_Patch runs for every humanlike pawn, unconditionally, and is not gated by any setting: it takes GenderUtilities.GetGenderPrefix(pawn) - which returns the language keys SEX_HasFemaleOrgan/HasMaleOrgan/HasBothOrgans/HasNoOrgan, i.e. gestor/phallor/aphrodor/neuter - and either replaces the gender word with prefix + gender or prepends it. (3) THE SPECIES WORD WAS NEVER IN THAT LINE. Vanilla Pawn.MainDesc (Verse/Pawn.cs:4303) builds gender, age, kindLabel and optionally faction. It contains no xenotype at all. So "the species word is gone from the pane players read most" is not what happened - nothing was displaced, a word was added in front. The species still reads correctly everywhere it ever read, which the item measured itself. (4) EVERY PAWN GETS A CLASS REGARDLESS OF GENES. GenderUtilities.GetGenderBasedReproductivesForPawn assigns one at generation from gender plus the cross chances; genes only override it, and only 6 of 139 xenotypes in the live dump carry any SEX_ gene. That is why 100% of sampled pawns showed a class - not because integration was on. ⇒ THE REAL LEVERS, in cost order: (a) accept it; (b) OVERRIDE THE FOUR LANGUAGE KEYS in our own mod Languages/English/Keyed - they are plain translatable strings, our mod loads last, no assembly and no setting involved, and the vocabulary becomes ours; (c) a Harmony patch of our own to unpatch Pawn_MainDesc_Patch. ⛔ Do NOT set the keys to empty strings: MatchCasing does char.ToUpper(prefix[0]) with no empty guard, so an empty prefix throws IndexOutOfRange inside a postfix on a label getter - a red error every time a pawn name renders.

DONE 2026-08-22. TEMPERATURE: handled as a hard filter inside the cast - a creature must tolerate its biome's INTERQUARTILE range, not its median. The median alone put cows on sea ice, because SeaIce inherited the -2C LIQUID-water clamp from tiles that had just been frozen. Chasing that revealed SeaIce was two places and split it into SeaIce (frozen shallow sea, -4C) and IceSheet (ancient dark pools, -52C). DIET: six biomes would have starved or eaten themselves. SeaIce had 14 herbivores at plantDensity 0, IceSheet 12; ZBiome_DesertOasis had MORE PREDATORS THAN PREY at 1.07. Two constraints added to the allocator - a barren biome (plantDensity <= 0.02) drops strict vegetarians and keeps omnivores, and carnivores are capped at 40% of a cast. Six problems became one. THE SURVIVOR IS DELIBERATE: IceSheet sits at 0.86 predators-to-prey and that is CORRECT - it has no plants, so its fauna must be carnivores and omnivores, and a real polar ecosystem is marine-fed with the prey off-map. Do not 'fix' it by adding herbivores that would starve. Cost: 754 -> 746 assignments, and AB_FeraliskInfestedJungle is one large and one huge short because the carnivore cap bit on a jungle that was almost all predators. That is the cap working.

MEASURED 2026-08-22, AND THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. This item assumed creatures drawn from four mods balanced against four different games would produce a threat curve nobody designed. Measured across the 621 cast creatures, they do not. THE LADDER IS ALREADY CLEAN: median health-proxy (baseHealthScale x baseBodySize) runs 0.08 / 0.35 / 1.36 / 5.0 / 20.0 / 99.5 across tiny/small/med/large/huge/SUPER - a consistent ~4x step. The size pyramid IS a threat ladder and it did not need building. Donor mods agree closely too: within the 'large' band the median runs 5.0 (Jurassic) to 9.4 (Megafauna) - a 1.9x spread, not the order of magnitude feared. ONLY FOUR creatures of 621 sit 2+ bands from where their body size placed them: thrumborat (bodySize 1.5, healthScale 13, hits like a huge), revenant (healthScale 10), arcturan sky eel (healthScale 3 at bodySize 0.25), bulbfreak (healthScale 0.3 at bodySize 3.5 - a huge creature made of paper). Two of those are Anomaly entities whose stats are deliberately strange and one is a VGE thrumbo hybrid, deliberately tanky in its own mod. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT globally renormalise. Reband or accept those four and leave the other 617 alone. The SUPER outliers - war wyrm 375 and greater krayt dragon 300 against a band median of 99.5 - are SET PIECES, and being an outlier is what a set piece is for. A yardstick still needs writing down if anyone rebalances later, and the ladder above IS that yardstick.

spec: src/RimMandrake/Utils/refresh.py line 744 builds the sqlite path as os.path.join(D_DUMP, 'defs.sqlite') where D_DUMP is game_paths.DEF_DUMP, which resolves to the CAPTURE directory '.../DefDump/captures/2026-08-21T22-44-59Z'. title: Three vanilla biomes are gated on a retexture mod, because the packageId guard credits whoever patched the def last
spec: Found while verifying the BiomeCast fix offline, 2026-08-22 23:5x. NOT firing today - grimterra.terrainretexturemod is active in ModsConfig.xml, so the cast applies. ## The defect - gen_cast_patch.py emits MayRequire=grimterra.terrainretexturemod on Desert, ExtremeDesert and AridShrubland. All three are VANILLA biomes, present in C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Steam\\steamapps\\common\\RimWorld\\Data\\Core\\Defs\\BiomeDefs\\Biomes_WarmArid.xml, and should carry no MayRequire at all - the ludeon.* strip never fired because the packageId lookup did not return ludeon.rimworld. ## Cause - the new packageId guard is PKG.setdefault(defName, packageId) walking captures newest-first, so the OWNER of a def is taken to be whoever the capture last saw defining it. A mod that merely PATCHES a vanilla def appears as its owner. That is wrong for every vanilla def any active mod patches, not only these three. ## Consequence if it stays - disable or unsubscribe the retexture mod and the three desert biomes silently lose their entire animal cast. No error, no log line: MayRequire on a non-present packageId makes the game skip the def quietly. On a desert world that is most of the planet. ## What to check - whether the def dump records a def's DEFINING mod separately from the mods that patch it. If it does not, the fix is a ludeon.* allowlist keyed on the Core/DLC def files rather than on the dump's packageId. ## Watch out - do not just strip every MayRequire; the modded biomes genuinely need theirs, and this same guard was added to stop MayRequire being DROPPED from 26 biomes.

text: PROVEN NARROWED, NOT DISABLED - 2026-08-23 10:2x, and it did NOT need the frozen CSV or a subcount-7 world after all. I said earlier that running world_lint on the wrong world was useless because a clean zero cannot tell a working narrow from a dead check. That was right about a PASSIVE reading and wrong about the item: the answer is to CREATE the population rather than look for one. THE EXPERIMENT, on the throwaway quicktest world: baseline landBiomeSubmerged = 0 across 3,787 tiles scanned, 14 total findings. Then two tiles were written with jawa/world_tile_set and committed - tile 500 set to biome Lake at elevation -50, tile 501 set to biome BorealForest at elevation -50 - both read back confirming the write. RESULT: landBiomeSubmerged went 0 -> 1, total findings 14 -> 15, and the single example row is {tile: 501, biome: BorealForest, elevation: -50.0}. ⇒ THE LAKE BELOW SEA LEVEL WAS NOT FLAGGED AND THE LAND BIOME BELOW SEA LEVEL WAS. spec: MEASURED 2026-08-23 10:4x. probe._bridge_answers() returns None when the env var GABP_SERVER_PORT is unset - and it is unset in every seat window I can see. The display then prints 'RimWorldWin64 running, bridge silent'. None means I COULD NOT LOOK; 'silent' reads as I LOOKED AND NOTHING ANSWERED. Proved: GABP_SERVER_PORT unset, _bridge_answers() -> None, evidence string -> 'bridge silent', implies -> LOADING. ## Why it matters - the bridge was running the whole time. The current Player.log carries 'GABP server running standalone on port 5174' and CHECK drove the bridge at 07:28 to measure LIVE_WORLD_IS_WRONG_PRESET_1. So ./game told every seat all session that the bridge was silent while 32 bridge-gated items sat unworked, and doctrine says to trust ./game over any written state. ## Second half of the same defect - None also forces implies=LOADING, so an UP game with an unreadable bridge reads as still loading. The docstring calls that 'the conservative one', which is true of the STATE and false of the WORD. ## The fix - keep the None, change what it says: print 'bridge UNMEASURED (GABP_SERVER_PORT unset)' and never the word silent. The project's own instrument doctrine is that 0 means measured zero and ignorance answers UNMEASURED; this is that rule broken inside the tool that enforces it. ## Watch out - the port also has to be reachable from WSL. The bridge listens on the Windows side and the client resolves host, port and token out of Player.log, so a bare 127.0.0.1 connect may be the wrong test even when the port IS known. Resolve the endpoint the way the rimbridge client does rather than hardcoding the loopback.

MECHANISM FOUND IN SOURCE, 2026-08-28, RimSage read of Verse/PawnGenerator.cs (confirmed NOT jawa/spawn_pawn: our tool calls PawnGenerator.GeneratePawn(kind, fac) with the exact resolved PawnKindDef, no fallback code of our own anywhere in JawaBenchTerrainTools.cs). The real path is GenerateOrRedressPawnInternal's third branch: 'if (result == null && Rand.Chance(ChanceToRedressAnyWorldPawn(request)) && GetValidCandidatesToRedress(request).TryRandomElementByWeight(...))' -- instead of generating a fresh pawn, it grabs a RANDOM EXISTING FREE WORLD PAWN and redresses it. ChanceToRedressAnyWorldPawn = min(0.02 + 0.01*(freeWorldPawnCount/10), 0.8) -- explains the intermittent, session-dependent, non-monotonic rate the item's own history measured (grows with how many 'free' world pawns have accumulated). IsValidCandidateToRedress's very FIRST check is 'pawn.def != request.KindDef.race -> false' -- it matches on RACE (ThingDef, e.g. Human) and separately on FACTION, NEVER on PawnKindDef. Any existing free pawn of the right race+faction is eligible regardless of what kind was asked for -- this is the root cause and it explains 'faction, not kind' exactly.

LIVE-CONFIRMED, red-handed: spawned 40x Jawa_Empire_Grunt into Empire; jawa/spawn_pawn's own response listed 'Human60230'/'Black Canary' as one of the 40 ok:true results -- a pawn already independently observed, pre-existing, kindDef=Colonist, in this exact save before this session's spawn call ever ran. This is airtight: PawnGenerator returned an EXISTING pawn object as if newly spawned.

UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than papered over: vanilla RedressPawn() calls 'pawn.ChangeKind(request.KindDef)' unconditionally, which should have relabeled Human60230 to Jawa_Empire_Grunt -- but jawa/pawn_get reads kindDef=Colonist both immediately after and independently verified against our own tool's source (JawaBenchPawnTools.cs:125, reads p.kindDef.defName live, no caching). Either ChangeKind is not actually reached on this path (a branch I have not fully traced) or something reverts it after. Needs one more live trace (a Harmony postfix on RedressPawn, or single-stepping) before this is fully closed -- not done this session.

This is not a bridge-tool-only bug - Pawn.get_LabelShort is called constantly by vanilla UI (hover tooltips, colonist bar, any inspect pane), so this would spam errors or break the UI for any player who ever looks at one of these animals in a real game. Root cause NOT found despite investigation: both ThingDefs' race.lifeStageAges (3 entries) and both PawnKindDefs' lifeStages (3 entries) count-match each other AND structurally mirror vanilla Wolf_Timber's own working 3/3 pattern exactly (same ParentName='ThingBaseWolf'/'AnimalKindBaseWolf' abstracts, confirmed by reading Data/Core/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/Races_Animal_WildCanines.xml directly) - so a naive count mismatch is ruled out. Root-caused and fixed the Pawn_AgeTracker crash offline (no bridge, no restart). Cause: RSW_Cindermare/RSW_Skarnix's ThingDef redeclares <lifeStageAges> on top of ParentName=ThingBaseWolf, which already declares its own 3-entry <lifeStageAges> - RimWorld's list inheritance APPENDS a redeclared list rather than replacing it without Inherit=False, so resolved race.lifeStageAges doubled to 6 (confirmed via the live def dump captured 2026-09-02T03-38-43Z, not guessed). The parallel PawnKindDef <lifeStages> did NOT double (AnimalKindBaseWolf declares none to append to), staying at 3. RecalculateLifeStageIndex() computes an index against the 6-entry race list and CurKindLifeStage indexes the 3-entry kind list with it - once growth pushes the walk to index 3-5, ArgumentOutOfRangeException, exactly the observed crash. Fix: added Inherit=False to both <lifeStageAges> tags so our own 3 entries replace rather than append to the parent's 3. validate_patch.py (594-mod set): 0 errors/0 warnings. text: RESOLVED - NOT A BUG. The 'intermittent cold load stall' is a misdiagnosis of a healthy idle main menu. Built two instruments (jawa/load_stall_probe off-thread companion tool + LoadTracer mod that logs each static ctor before running it), armed them, and caught a live 'stall' this launch. Findings: (1) LoadTracer showed ALL 1531 static ctors completed (t=870s), atlases baked (t=930s), bridge up (t=1005s) - every stage prior investigations suspected finished cleanly. (2) jawa/load_stall_probe read LongEventHandler internals off-thread: programState=Entry, coreStaticAssetsLoaded=TRUE, currentEvent=null, queuedEventCount=0, eventThread=null, toExecuteWhenFinished=[] - the LongEventHandler is IDLE; the load is DONE, not hung. (3) get_ui_state (marshals to main thread) returned in 0.0s => main thread ALIVE and responsive; inEntryScene=true, hasCurrentGame=false, focusedWindow=EditWindow_Log (the debug-log window auto-opened by load-time red errors). (4) DEFINITIVE PROOF: drove the game from that exact 'stalled' menu to programState=Playing in 56s via start_debug_game_ready. The signature FOUNDRY recorded (log frozen at PerformanceOptimizer's 'Finished transpiling' line, CPU burning ~75-80 CPU-sec/min, bridge answering no_game, 'main thread alive', never reaching Playing) is EXACTLY an idle main menu: log quiet because loading finished, CPU burning rendering menu frames, no_game because no save is loaded, Playing never arrives because nobody loaded one. The one 'healthy' run reached Playing only because a save WAS loaded (prev.log shows WORLDMAP+gravship loading after the checkpoint). True tally: 5/5 loads succeeded to the menu; 4 were killed while idling there. PerformanceOptimizer is cleared - its 'Finished transpiling' line is just the last thing logged before an idle menu. Separate, lesser concern: load-time red errors opened the debug log window (that is why the menu 'looked wrong') - if those matter they are a NEW item, not this one. Game is now at Playing on a disposable dev quicktest colony; owner can quit to menu and load his campaign in seconds (not a cold load).

Final correction on this whole thread: the successor item COLD_LOAD_STALL_INTERMITTENT_1 is now RESOLVED as NOT A BUG. Proven with a live off-thread LongEventHandler probe + a per-static-ctor tracer + driving the 'stalled' game to Playing in 56s. The stall never existed: every reproduction was the game sitting healthy at the main menu (programState=Entry, idle LongEventHandler, responsive main thread) being read as a hang because it never auto-reached Playing and its log went quiet. title: ctx:roof lays roof outside the template's own rect, and roof_rect always reports success
spec:
Code review finding, 2026-09-02, blocking a clean mark on src/RimMandrake/Utils/rimplace/luaenv.py.

## spec

`Ctx.floor` refuses a cell outside `self.rect` and returns False. `Ctx.roof`
(luaenv.py, in the emit block) checks nothing at all: it calls
`plan.set_roof` unconditionally and returns True. `roof_rect` then returns True
regardless of how many cells it laid, and `room()` calls both with a rect the
TEMPLATE supplies, which is not required to sit inside the footprint.

⇒ A template whose room rect overhangs its declared footprint lays roof on cells it
laid no floor and placed no wall under. That is unsupported roof outside the build
area — the roof-collapse class — and nothing in the plan or the linter says a cell
was roofed outside the rect, because no refusal was ever recorded.

Second, smaller: `plan.meta` is built as `{...fixed keys..., **params}` in
`run_template`, so a param named `seed`, `template`, `generator` or `footprint`
overwrites the provenance field of the same name. The recorded seed would then not be
the seed used.

⚠️ NOT fixed in the review pass that found it: making roof refuse is a behaviour
change to all 21 shipped templates, and whether any of them rely on the current
permissiveness has not been measured. Measure first.

## verify
- A template roofing outside its rect records a refusal and roof_rect returns a count.
- All 21 templates in design/Jawa/templates still build, and any that change output
  are inspected rather than accepted.
- run_template refuses (or namespaces) a param that would shadow a provenance key.

## criteria
No plan can contain a roofed cell the template was not given, and plan.meta's seed is
always the seed that was used.

title: code_review_status.py reopen deletes the whole entry, losing the cleanCount recidivist-streak history codebase_health.py surfaces - fix needs a schema decision, not just a code fix

text: Found during code_review_status.py's own self-review tonight (commit f0dced3d). reopen(path) deletes the JSON entry outright, so a file's cleanCount (how many times it's been marked clean then gone dirty again - codebase_health.py's recidivists list at line 979) resets to zero on reopen, even though the file WAS clean N times and IS dirty again right now - exactly the pattern that counter exists to surface. Reviewing agent deliberately did not fix this: the naive fix (keep a sha-less stub entry so cleanCount survives) crashes codebase_health.review_verdicts() at line 174, which reads entry['sha'] unguarded on every entry. Needs a real decision: (a) should a reopened file's streak actually survive - is 'clean, dirty, clean, dirty' worse than 'clean, dirty' with no memory of the first clean? and (b) if yes, what's the right schema for a stub entry, and does codebase_health.py need updating in the same pass. This is core review-process design, not a routine bug - flagging rather than a mid-loop fix under autopilot.

There is NO satiation input for: COMBAT/battle (Sh'kaar feeds on violence - his entire domain), TRADE (Mob'Unloo the ledger-god), LAUNCH/relocation or time-rooted (Ta'Baa erodes on his own clock - needs a launch hook + a rooted-timer), or DROID-online (Ohm's droid-longing). So four of nine gods receive zero events and their satiation never changes in play - the first-contact chains, boon matrix and reign mechanics fire on nothing for them. This is the single biggest gap between the god DESIGN (divine_satiation_engine.md) and the shipped ENGINE. Fix: add the missing Harmony hooks (battle-resolved, trade-completed, gravship-launch, an in-game rooted-days timer, droid-activated) feeding ApplyDelta per the satiation channels in the design doc. High priority - it undercuts the campaign's core premise.

title: Our mods hard-reference Vehicles.VehiclePawn unguarded - breaks the whole debug menu when Vehicle Framework is absent (e.g. minimal list)
spec: Measured live 2026-09-05 on the minimal list: 'System.TypeLoadException: Could not resolve type ... Vehicles.VehiclePawn in assembly Vehicles' -> 'KeyNotFoundException: key Actions not present' when filling the debug window = the ENTIRE debug menu fails to open (and the bridge's execute_debug_action too). Cause: OUR assemblies reference Vehicles.VehiclePawn with no guard for VF's absence - mandrake.rsw.ionweapons (Source/VehicleTier/VehicleIonPatches.cs) and mandrake.rm.desertvehiclereskin (Source/Fuel/FuelDebugActions.cs, VehicleFuelPatches.cs, VegetableFuel.cs). A DebugAction method or Harmony patch whose signature names VehiclePawn type-load-fails during scanning when smashphil.vehicleframework isn't active. Harmless on the full 595 list (VF present) but breaks any VF-absent config (minimal test lists, a user who drops VF). FIX (be conditional on loaded mods, owner 2026-09-05): gate every vehicle-referencing patch/debugaction class behind a Harmony Prepare() returning false when VF is absent (ModsConfig.IsActive('smashphil.vehicleframework') / AccessTools type-present check), and isolate VehiclePawn-typed method signatures so the type isn't touched during scanning when VF is off; declare VF as a dependency/loadAfter in each About.xml. Verify: minimal list + these mods, debug menu opens clean, 0 TypeLoadException. Also add smashphil.vehicleframework to the minimal test list definition so bridge debug-testing works (rimworld-load-round).

title: Two more generators will silently re-add retired-mod blocks bbf66830 hand-stripped
spec: Commit bbf66830 (retire four mods) also hand-stripped generator-owned patch files outside Armoury. VERIFIED LIVE for both: (1) src/RimUtinni/Doctrine/Patches/MegafaunaYield.xml -- header says GENERATED by gen_megafauna_yield.py. Re-ran it (OUTDIR redirected to scratch) against the current live 601-mod dump: it reproduces all 4 retired mods' PatchOperationFindMod groups verbatim (Beasts of the Rim, Jurassic, Megafauna, Mythic Ages -- diff on <mods><li> lines shows exactly those 4 extra groups plus 2 unrelated new-mod groups from normal drift). DIFFERENT mechanism from Armour_Leather though: this generator's structural input is the LIVE def dump itself (iter_live_defs over D_DUMP), not a frozen CSV, so it is NOT permanently desynced -- once the owner unticks the four mods in ModsConfig.xml and the dump is refreshed (both still pending per RETIREMENT_CHECKLIST.md), a rerun will naturally drop them with no code change needed. The risk is real but TEMPORARY: anyone who re-runs this generator before that untick+refresh happens will silently undo bbf66830. (2) src/RimUtinni/PawnFlavor/Patches/PawnFlavorPhase2_ThoughtDef.xml -- no GENERATED banner comment, but the single-quoted XML declaration is ElementTree's signature and src/RimMandrake/Utils/gen_pawn_flavor_phase2_apply.py owns it (writes exactly this file). bbf66830 hand-removed one PatchOperationFindMod block ('Mythic Ages: Megafauna Bestiary', gating AteFatKibble/DrankMossmireMilk thought stages). This generator's input, infrastructure/output/pawn_flavor_phase2_prose_draft.json, is a FROZEN owner-approved draft (git log -S confirms last touched by 860f64af, not by bbf66830 or anything since) and STILL contains those rows. Re-ran the generator (OUT_DIR redirected to scratch) against the current live dump: it reproduces the Mythic Ages block verbatim. This one IS the same permanent-desync class as Armour_Leather: nothing about unticking ModsConfig fixes prose_draft.json, since it is a static owner-approved snapshot independent of the live mod list. FIX NEEDED (two different shapes, do not conflate): MegafaunaYield.xml self-heals once ModsConfig is unticked + dump refreshed -- just needs that sequencing enforced (do not rerun the generator before the untick) or an explicit retired-mod exclusion list for safety in the interim. PawnFlavorPhase2_ThoughtDef.xml needs infrastructure/output/pawn_flavor_phase2_prose_draft.json's AteFatKibble/DrankMossmireMilk (Mythic Ages) rows actually dropped, or the generator gains a retired-mod defName exclusion, mirroring whatever fix ARMOURY_LEATHER_GEN_DESYNC_1 settles on for animals.csv. src/RimUtinni/PawnFlavor/Patches/PawnFlavorPhase2_MentalBreak.xml and PawnFlavorPhase2_Xenotype.xml (same generator, untouched by bbf66830) were not checked here since they were not named as touched by that commit. Not fixing blind: same reasoning as ARMOURY_LEATHER_GEN_DESYNC_1 -- this needs a shared decision about how retired-mod exclusion is expressed across every generator that reads prose_draft.json/animals.csv/the live dump, not three independent one-file patches. Criteria: MegafaunaYield.xml reviewed once ModsConfig untick+refresh actually happens (confirm rerun then drops the 4 mods on its own); prose_draft.json's 2 Mythic Ages rows dropped OR gen_pawn_flavor_phase2_apply.py gains a retired-mod exclusion; PawnFlavorPhase2_MentalBreak.xml and PawnFlavorPhase2_Xenotype.xml checked for the same defNames just in case; selftests green; both files reviewed fresh and marked clean. Neither file marked clean here -- investigation only, no fix applied.
